newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Orient-Avia sees new routes this year.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Orient-Avia sees new routes this year.

text.p: Private Russian airline Orient-Avia said on Thursday that it would open new international and domestic routes this year.

Company spokeswoman Yevgeniya Semerikova said the carrier planned to make scheduled flights from Moscow to Volgograd and Krasnodar later this year. "We also plan to open a passenger service to Moscow-Chisinau, the Moldovan capital," she said.
Semerikova said Orient-Avia planned to begin Moscow-Santa Domingo, Dominican Republic, scheduled flights via Shannon, Ireland. "The first technical flight is expected later this month," she added.
Semerikova said the company wanted to increase its aircraft fleet to lease two wide-body Ilyushin Il-86 passenger jets.
"We need a few planes because the demand for carrying passengers and cargo is increasing," she said.
The company's fleet consists of six aircraft, including four Ilyushin-62M long-range jets, one Ilyushin-86 wide-body plane and one Tupolev-134 jet.
Orient-Avia carried 161,000 passengers and 1,560 tonnes of cargo and mail in 1996, up from 95,800 passengers and 860 tonnes of cargo and mail in 1995.

Orient-Avia already has a regular service between Moscow and Vladivostok and Petropalovsk-Kamchatsky in the Russian Far East. The company, which was founded in 1994, also operates on the Moscow-Kaunas route.
